data.gender_notes: Dorthea is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Dorthea was a goddess of fertility and the protector of childbirth. In the Christian tradition, the name Dorthea is derived from the Greek word 'doron,' meaning 'gift.' The name is thus a reminder of the gift of life that God bestows upon us. The name Dorthea carries the meaning “Gift of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Dorthea usually hope their child will grow to embody gift of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.name: Δοροθέα
in_greek.meaning: Δωρεά του Θεού, ισχυρή και μεγάλη
in_greek.long_meaning: Η Δοροθέα είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'δωρεά' (δώρο) και 'θέα' (Θεός). Το όνομα αυτό ήταν γνωστό από την αρχαιότητα και συμβολίζει τη χάρη και την ευλογία του Θεού. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, η Δοροθέα θεωρείται σύμβολο της πνευματικής γενναιότητας και της αρετής.

in_latin.name: Dorothea
in_latin.meaning: Gift of God, strong and great
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Dorothea originates from the Greek words 'doros' (gift) and 'thea' (God). It was adopted into Latin as 'Dorothea' and became a popular name among early Christians. The name signifies divine favor and blessing, reflecting the Christian values of spiritual generosity and devotion. Throughout history, Dorothea has been associated with several Christian saints and martyrs.

in_english.name: Dorthea
in_english.long_meaning: The name Dorthea, derived from the Greek 'Δοροθέα' (Dorothea), means 'gift of God' or 'divine present.' It combines 'doron' (gift) and 'thea' (God). Historically, Dorthea has been used in Christian traditions to signify a child as a blessing from God. The name has been borne by several saints and has remained popular in various Christian cultures due to its spiritual significance and positive connotations.
